nodes.name: NiFeCo Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 5 mmol urea and 4 mmol NH4F were dissolved in 36 mL of ultrapure water and stirred until completely dissolved. Then, adding NF (4 cm × 2 cm) into the solution, and transferred to 50 mL stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave. Ultimately, the autoclave was airtight heated at 180°C lasting for 10 h followed by cooling down to room temperature naturally. Then wash with a lot of water and ethanol respectively, and dry at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: NiFeCo-E Etching Treatment
nodes.procedure: The NiFeCo (1 cm × 2 cm) was immersed in a 10 mL NaOH solution (5 M), and then the solution was heated to 90 °C in an oil bath for 10 min and kept for 90 min. Subsequently, the samples were washed and dried with water and ethanol.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows nanosheet morphology of Pt@NiFeCo-E on NF substrate, similar to Ni-based LDHs with or without treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b presents the nanosheet morphology of Pt@NiFeCo-E on the NF substrate, which is similar to the morphologies of the Ni-based LDHs with or without treatment (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacing of 0.26 nm assigned to (012) planes of NiFeLDH and 0.15 nm to (111) plane of Ni(OH)₂ in NiFeCo-E support of Pt@NiFeCo-E.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both the high resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) (Fig. 1c and S2) and XRD characterizations (Fig. 1d) reveal that the NiFeCo-E is composed of NiFe(Co)-LDH and Ni(Co)(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show Ni-Fe(Co) LDH (PDF#40-0215) and Ni(OH)₂ (PDF#14-0117) phases; diffraction peak at 11.4° (003) plane of Ni-Fe(Co) LDH shifts left after Pt anchoring indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns (Fig. 1d) reveal that the Ni-based LDHs before and after treatment were composed of Ni-Fe(Co) LDH (PDF#40-0215) and Ni(OH)₂ (PDF#14-0117), which is consistent with the TEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS elemental mapping demonstrates homogeneous dispersion of Co, Fe, Ni, O, and Pt elements in Pt@NiFeCo-E.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical compositions (Table S1) and the EDS mapping of Pt@NiFeCo-E (Fig. 1e) all demonstrated the homogeneously dispersion of Co, Fe, Ni, O, and Pt elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms 2Pt dimers (2.6 Å interatomic distance, 73.3%) and Pt₂ pairs (0.9 Å) evenly dispersed in Pt@NiFeCo-E; Pt on non-vacancy Pt@NiFeCo forms clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM (Fig. 1f and S4) analyses on different regions confirmed the 2Pt dimer and Pt₂ pair structure evenly dispersed in Pt@NiFeCo-E catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Eg1 (459 cm⁻¹), Alg (520 cm⁻¹) Ni-O(H) vibrations; new peak at 596 cm⁻¹ in etched samples indicates hydroxyl vibration near defect sites confirming cation vacancies; Pt loading shifts peaks to higher wavenumbers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a presents the Raman spectra collected on both the unloaded and Pt loaded NiFeCo and NiFeCo-E. In NiFeCo-E substrate, two representative peaks located at 459 and 520 cm⁻¹ could be assigned to the Eg1 bending vibration and the Alg stretching vibration modes...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Pt 4f peaks in Pt@NiFeCo-E at 71.00/74.35 eV (Pt⁰), 72.70/76.05 eV (Pt²⁺), 74.70/77.95 eV (Pt⁴⁺) with positive shifts vs Pt@NiFeCo due to cation vacancies; Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ (855.72/873.36 eV), Ni³⁺ (856.90/874.91 eV); Fe 2p shows 0.35 eV negative shift for Fe³⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Pt@NiFeCo-E, the peaks located at the binding energies of 71.00 and 74.35 eV assign to Pt 4f_{7/2} and Pt 4f_{5/2} of Pt^0 species (Fig. 2b), and we attribute two peaks of 72.70 and 76.05 eV to Pt 4f_{7/2} and Pt 4f_{5/2} of Pt^{2+} species. Meanwhile, the Pt^{4+} species are also affirmed by another two peaks at 74.70 and 77.95 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES white line between Pt foil and PtO₂ indicates Pt oxidation state 0 to +4 in Pt@NiFeCo-E; Ni k-edge between +2/+3; higher energy shifts in Pt@NiFeCo-E confirm increased oxidation states from vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Pt L₃-edge XANES spectra (Fig. 2c), the white line position of Pt@NiFeCo-E situates between those of the Pt foil and the PtO₂, indicating that the oxidation state of the Pt atoms in Pt@NiFeCo-E is between 0 and +4, which agrees well with the XPS analyses.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Pt loading 9.04 wt% in Pt@NiFeCo-E; Ni:Fe:Co = 5:1:1 in NiFeCo-LDH, 4.6:1:1 in NiFeCo-E (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass loading of the Pt species (Table S1) in Pt@NiFeCo-E was determined to be 9.04 wt.% by an ICP-OES method, revealing the adsorption affinity of NiFeCo-E substrate towards Pt atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines Cdl = 16.81 mF cm⁻² for Pt@NiFeCo-E (highest), indicating more catalytically active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the electrochemical active surface areas of the catalysts were evaluated by measuring the Cdl values (Fig. 3c and S16). Again, the Pt@NiFeCo-E possessed the highest Cdl value (16.81 mF cm⁻²)...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistance Rct = 3.84 Ω for Pt@NiFeCo-E (HER) and 0.98 Ω (OER), validating fastest electron transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S15a, the Nyquist plot shows that the Pt@NiFeCo-E possessed the lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct, 3.84 Ω)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt EXAFS in Pt@NiFeCo-E shows Pt-O at 1.77 Å and Pt-M (Fe/Co/Ni/Pt) at 2.52 Å; WT contour plots confirm Pt-O (~1.8 Å⁻¹) and Pt-M (~2.5 Å⁻¹) coordinations ruling out Pt clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2d, Pt in Pt@NiFeCo-E has two prominent peaks, which are attributed to the Pt-O and the Pt-M (Fe, Co, Ni and Pt) at 1.77 Å and 2.52 Å, respectively.
